'''Eric A. Slover'''<ref name="CMOHS-2026">{{cite web |date=25 February 2026 |title=Eric A Slover Venezuela Medal of Honor citation |url=https://www.cmohs.org/recipients/eric-a-slover |access-date=25 February 2026 |website=www.cmohs.org|publisher=Congressional Medal of Honor Society}}</ref> is a [[United States Army]] [[Chief Warrant Officer 5]] (CW5) who received the [[Medal of Honor]] for his actions during [[2026 United States intervention in Venezuela|Operation Absolute Resolve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stilwell |first=Blake |date=24 February 2026 |title=An Army pilot shot three times during the Maduro Raid just received the Medal of Honor |url=https://www.wearethemighty.com/history/eric-slover-medal-of-honor/ |access-date=25 February 2026 |website=We Are The Mighty |language=en-US}}</ref> During the operation, Slover was a [[Boeing CH-47 Chinook|MH-47 Chinook]] pilot in the [[160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment (Airborne)]], colloquially known as the Night Stalkers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schogol |first1=Jeff |title=Trump awards Medals of Honor to Maduro raid and Korean War pilots |url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/military-medals-of-honor-2026/ |access-date=26 February 2026 |work=Task & Purpose |date=25 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Tom |title=US 'Night Stalkers' seen in Caribbean as fears of regime change rise in Venezuela |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/oct/22/us-night-stalkers-caribbean-fears-regime-change-venezuela-nicolas-maduro |access-date=26 February 2026 |work=The Guardian |date=22 October 2025}}</ref>  Slover is the first and only CW5 in history to receive the Medal of Honor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Army - Medal of Honor Recipients - U.S. Military Awards for Valor - Top 3 |url=https://valor.defense.gov/Recipients/Army-Medal-of-Honor-Recipients/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260109130834/https://valor.defense.gov/Recipients/Army-Medal-of-Honor-Recipients/ |archive-date=2026-01-09 |access-date=2026-03-21 |website=valor.defense.gov |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Military career ==

Slover enlisted in the Army in 2005. After completing basic training, he attended [[Warrant Officer]] Candidate School and flight school, becoming a [[Boeing CH-47 Chinook|Chinook]] helicopter pilot.<ref name=Toropin>{{cite news |last1=Toropin |first1=Konstantin |title=Army pilot wounded in Maduro raid gets Medal of Honor during Trump's speech |url=https://apnews.com/article/state-of-union-maduro-venezuela-wounded-pilot-69c70a7385ec14f58a84a4a7e4557c08 |access-date=26 February 2026 |work=AP News |date=25 February 2026 |language=en |archive-date=25 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260225144624/https://apnews.com/article/state-of-union-maduro-venezuela-wounded-pilot-69c70a7385ec14f58a84a4a7e4557c08 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Afghanistan===
{{further|War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)}}
While assisting in a medical evacuation in [[Badghis Province]] in November 2009 with the [[82nd Airborne Division]], a helicopter Slover was piloting was pierced by a [[rocket-propelled grenade]]. The munition failed to explode and remained in the helicopter for the duration of the flight. After landing, Slover was the first off the Chinook to get explosives experts and help for the wounded. This medical evacuation mission was described in 2009 as one of the "biggest of the Afghan War".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Price |first1=Jay |title=Army evacuation came within inches of disaster |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/baker-city-herald-army-evacuation-came-w/192129445/ |access-date=25 February 2026 |work=Baker City Herald |date=16 November 2009 |pages=6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2009-11-16 |title=Rescue came within inches of disaster |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/news-and-record-rescue-came-within-inche/192193490/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |work=News and Record |pages=7}}</ref>

=== Operation Absolute Resolve ===
{{further|2026 United States intervention in Venezuela}}
During the American raid that captured Venezuelan President [[Nicolás Maduro]], Slover was the flight lead in the cockpit of the first helicopter, a MH-47 Chinook. The helicopter came under severe machine-gun fire and Slover was hit four times in his leg and hip. Maintaining control of the aircraft despite his wounds, Slover safely landed the helicopter, allowing the operation to continue. Slover was awarded the [[Medal of Honor]] by US President [[Donald Trump]] at the [[2026 State of the Union Address]].<ref name=Noury>{{cite news |last1=Noury |first1=Tanya |title=Army helicopter pilot wounded during Maduro raid receives Medal of Honor during State of the Union |url=https://www.militarytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2026/02/25/army-helicopter-pilot-wounded-during-maduro-raid-receives-medal-of-honor-during-state-of-the-union/ |access-date=25 February 2026 |work=Military Times |date=25 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Slover was one of two men to receive the Medal of Honor during the address, alongside the 100-year-old [[US Navy]] Captain [[E. Royce Williams]], a [[Korean War]] veteran.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-awards-back-to-back-medals-honor-during-state-union-address|title=Trump awards back-to-back Medals of Honor during State of the Union address|first=Amanda|last=Macias|publisher=[[Fox News]]|website=foxnews.com|date=25 February 2026|access-date=25 February 2026|archive-date=25 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260225061839/https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-awards-back-to-back-medals-honor-during-state-union-address|url-status=live}}</ref> This was the first time the Medal of Honor was awarded at a State of the Union Address.<ref>{{Cite web |last=CBS News |date=2026-02-24 |title=Trump awards Medal of Honor to 100-year-old veteran during State of the Union - CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/state-of-the-union-2026-trump-royce-williams-medal-of-honor/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Medal of Honor citation ===
{{Blockquote|Chief Warrant Officer Five Eric A. Slover distinguished himself by conspicuous gallantry and intrepidity, above and beyond the call of duty, on January 3, 2026, during a mission in Venezuela, in support of Operation Absolute Resolve. Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover piloted his MH-47 as the lead aircraft of the operation, tasked with executing a highly complex infiltration through hostile Integrated Air Defense Systems to safely deliver military forces. During ingress, Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover skillfully led the helicopter force through a dense jungle valley in a mountainous region, navigating marginal weather conditions, numerous topographical hazards, and near insurmountable surface to air threats. Upon touching down at the designated landing zone, Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover’s aircraft was immediately engaged by multiple machine gun positions at close range. The hostile fire resulted in 15 armor-piercing rounds entering his cockpit, with four rounds striking his leg. Despite the intense and effective enemy fire, and at great personal risk, Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover maintained his situational awareness and aircraft’s position in the line of fire to ensure the safe infiltration of the military forces. After the force disembarked, and despite suffering significant life-threatening injuries, Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover identified hostile heavy machine gun positions that were engaging his aircraft and targeting the ground forces. He maneuvered his aircraft to enable his door gunner to deliver effective fire, successfully neutralizing the threats. Chief Warrant Officer Five Slover’s heroic actions undoubtedly saved countless American lives and ensured the complete and overwhelming success of the mission. His gallantry under fire and extraordinary valor are in keeping with the highest traditions of military service and reflect great credit upon himself and the United States Army.<ref name="CMOHS-2026" />}}

== Personal life ==
Slover is a graduate of the College of Graduate and Continuing Studies at [[Norwich University]] located in [[Northfield, Vermont]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.norwich.edu/news/warrior-scholar-cw5-eric-slovers-medal-honor-embodies-norwich-spirit |title=The Warrior Scholar: CW5 Eric Slover's Medal of Honor Embodies the Norwich Spirit |publisher=Norwich University Marketing & Communications Office |website=norwich.edu |date=February 25, 2026 |accessdate=February 25, 2026}}</ref> His wife, Amy, blessed his [[dog tag]]s with [[holy water]] before the mission. <ref>{{cite news |last1=Gill |first1=Benjamin |title=Trump Gives Medal of Honor to Wounded Warrior Hero of Venezuela Op |url=https://cbn.com/news/us/trump-gives-medal-honor-wounded-warrior-hero-venezuela-op |access-date=26 February 2026 |work=CBN |date=25 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Trump Awards Helicopter Pilot and Devout Catholic Highest Medal |url=https://www.catholic365.com/article/58647/trump-awards-helicopter-pilot-and-devout-catholic-highest-medal.html |access-date=5 March 2026 |work=The Catholic Philadelphian |publisher=Catholic365 |language=en}}</ref>
